claims.text: The damaged high-value component is made from a material with high hot-cracking susceptibility.
Laser-based cold-welding repair can mitigate hot-cracking risk in the component.
Laser-based cold-welding repair can enable the damaged component to remain in service under aggressive operating conditions.
Laser-based cold-welding has lower heat input than traditional fusion-welding repair.
The lower heat input reduces thermal distortion.
The lower heat input reduces residual stresses.
Reduced thermal distortion and residual stresses improve resistance to hot cracking.
Laser-based cold-welding repair will provide greater hot-cracking resistance than traditional fusion-welding repair.
Laser-based cold-welding repair will extend service life relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The relevant operating regime includes high temperature, high pressure, and cyclic loading.
The two repair methods can be compared using microstructural analysis, mechanical testing, and performance evaluation.
A higher hot-cracking incidence or shorter service life for laser-based cold-welding than for traditional fusion-welding under the specified conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
